fi-acreichthys-tomentosus.title: Aiptasia Eating Filefish
fi-acreichthys-tomentosus.summary: A small, camouflaged filefish from the Indo-West Pacific, widely kept to eat pest Aiptasia anemones. It can change color and texture to blend in.
rows: About 5.5 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Omnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, brine shrimp, chopped shrimp, squid and scallop, clam, krill, marine algae, marine pellets
Indo-West Pacific: Sri Lanka eastward thorough Indonesia to New Caledonia, north to southern Japan
notes: Once the Aiptasia is gone some individuals start picking at corals, polyps and other sessile invertebrates, so watch it closely in a reef.

fi-cantherhines-macrocerus.title: American Whitespotted Filefish
fi-cantherhines-macrocerus.summary: A large Caribbean filefish that feeds on sponges, gorgonians and algae in the wild. It is not reef safe and grows far too big for most home aquariums.
rows: Often seen in pairs in the wild
Omnivore: nori and other algae plus meaty foods such as mysis, krill and brine shrimp; eats sponges in the wild
Western Atlantic: Florida and Bermuda to Brazil
notes: Will eat shrimp, crabs, small clams and snails.

fi-paraluteres-prionurus.title: Mimic Filefish (Valentini Mimic)
fi-paraluteres-prionurus.summary: A harmless filefish that copies the look of the toxic saddled (Valentini) puffer to avoid predators. Small and shy, it may nibble corals if not fed enough.
rows: Shy; may argue with its own kind
Singly or in pairs (sometimes small groups in the wild)
Only with care: well-fed fish usually leave corals alone, but may nip soft corals, LPS and tubeworms
Meaty foods (mysis, brine shrimp) plus algae such as nori and spirulina, fed several times a day
notes: Give it hiding places and calm tankmates.

fi-pseudalutarius-nasicornis.title: Rhino Filefish (Rhinoceros Leatherjacket)
fi-pseudalutarius-nasicornis.summary: A slim, pale brown filefish with two brown stripes and a long "horn" spine on its head; adults pick up yellow spots. It lives on weedy, sandy lagoon and coastal reefs, often in pairs.
rows: Large: about 220 gal (1,000 L) is recommended
Use caution: it eats small crustaceans and other tiny invertebrates
Omnivore: algae plus small meaty foods such as mysis, brine shrimp, krill, copepods and amphipods
Indo-West Pacific, from South Africa to Japan and eastern Australia
notes: Often found in pairs in the wild.
